newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wave of pre-dawn arson attacks hits Macau.
newsitem.headline: Wave of pre-dawn arson attacks hits Macau.

text.p: Dozens of vehicles were set on fire in a wave of arson attacks in the Portuguese-administered territory of Macau on Tuesday, Hong Kong government radio reported.
The attacks destroyed nine motorcycles in a carpark outside Macau's traffic police headquarters and damaged 13 others just before dawn, the radio said.
Six other vehicles were set ablaze on the island of Taipa, one of Macau's three main land masses, and in the middle and northern parts of the enclave, it said.
Around the same time, six shots were fired but it was not clear whether the shots were related to the arson attacks.

The attacks were the latest in a string of violent incidents, including bombings and shootings, which have been attributed to turf wars between rival triad gangsters vying for control of rackets linked to Macau's thriving casino industry.
The territory of 440,000 people, under Portuguese rule for the past four and a half centuries, reverts to China in 1999, two years after its neighbour, the British colony of Hong Kong.
